dedupe_keys.name: pyam energy and climate scenario analysis

description: pyam is a Python package for checking, analysing and visualizing integrated-assessment and energy-system scenarios. Its developers support tables of model, scenario, region, variable, unit and year values. The JOSS paper describes analysis of climate and human-environment model ensembles; the current own README explicitly includes macro-energy and sectoral studies. The public repository reports Apache-2.0, so the software is free. Spatial and temporal coverage depend on the supplied model output, from national regions to global aggregates and from historical years through projected decades. Energy modellers can compare generation, fuel, emissions or demand pathways and inspect consistency across scenarios. A caveat is that pyam analyses output; it does not itself simulate a grid, verify model assumptions or resolve subregional asset impacts. Differing variable definitions and units can invalidate a comparison if left unchecked. No directly related catalogue record was found. The article and own repository were read without obtaining scenario databases or executing analysis.
name: pyam energy and climate scenario analysis
